Samira: Quick q from today's all-hands: leadership mentioned a 'holiday ramp plan' and a 'canary routing lane' for capacity. Can someone give a concise explanation we can use in PM/CS comms?

Ben: Short explainer: holiday ramp = intentionally overprovisioned warm capacity we spin up ahead of known peak windows (holidays/major product launches). Canary routing lane = a lightweight, low-latency path that handles a small percentage of traffic using prewarmed kernels to validate config before ramping fully. Canary is used to detect regressions early.

Hannah: For CS: what does this mean for customers if procurement delays push racks back? We need copy for status updates.

Liu: Procurement note: we maintain a rolling set of near-term leases and spot fallback to cover 3-6 weeks of variance. If rack delivery slips, the order we use is: 1) use canary lane/optimized variants, 2) increase holiday ramp utilization, 3) remap reserved commitments, 4) cross-region spill if sustained.

Samira: Can we get concrete expected latency deltas for each step so PMs can set expectations?

Ben: Numbers (very conservative): canary/optimized variants -> +30-120ms p99; ramp utilization increase -> +50-200ms p99 for a short window; remapped reserved buckets -> +80-300ms depending on distance; cross-region spill -> +150-500ms worst-case. We try to avoid quality regressions by preferring fidelity-tested quantized variants.

Hannah: Pasteable blurb for status pages please?

Ben: Blurb: "We're proactively preparing extra warm capacity and a canary routing lane ahead of peak windows. If hardware delivery is delayed, we'll route traffic through optimized pathways and reserved capacity to preserve responsiveness; you may see small, temporary increases in latency while we maintain SLAs. Reserved customers will be prioritized."

Samira: Ops/Runbook snippet for teams to link in communications?

Ben: Tiny ops snippet below, full runbook in Confluence.

```
# holiday/canary fallback snippet
on delivery.delay:
  enable_canary_lane(percent=5)
  route -> optimized_variant(timeout=2m)
  increase_holiday_ramp(util=+25%)
  remap_reserved_buckets(if sustained>=15m)
  consider_cross_region_spill(duration>=30m)
  notify #infra #support #cs
```

Liu: I'll push an updated ETA matrix to the roadmap (expected rack arrivals + lease renewals). If any delivery slips >7 days, we'll start canary + ramp immediately.

Hannah: CS action: please export customer tag CSV (reserved/prewarm-eligible/canary-eligible) and drop in #cs. We'll prep outbound comms for high-risk accounts.

StatusBot: Runbook page created: https://confluence.redwood/infra/holiday-canary-runbook :white_check_mark:

Samira: Thanks! Action items: Ben to link runbook in the all-hands notes, Liu to publish ETA matrix by EOD Thu, Hannah to share CSV and draft comms. I'll coordinate leadership sign-off on the public blurb. :thumbsup:
